[quote=skullsbrough;60369971][b] Preperations for an Expedition | Erene2000 | Second Flouesch Republic[/b]

"Muller!"

[i]Gonthier Fuelenger says, approaching Müller with a stack of papers in his hands. He was the new Secretariat of National Defense after Marc Ewen resigned after he was expelled from the Radical Republican Party for supposedly collaborating with royalists and lying about his previous association with them. [/i]

"Fuelenger. You're supposed to address me as consul." Muller says, sighing, Fuelenger had been his suggestion after all

"Chill out muller. This whole republic thing was supposed to make us all equal. You aren't special! 

Anyway. I have the great plan I talked to you about to get us more crude oil. See, there are these islands."

He pulls out a satellite data map of the islands

"They're so irrelevant actually, that I couldn't find a name for what they're actually called. Muller, can you believe that? I don't even think people actually live there either." 

"So what are you suggesting here. Fuelenger" Muller looks over the map before looking back up at Fuelenger, his interest is piqued at least. Especially since Müller had been wanting to create a new source of income before he introduced his National Republic Fund to the Staatsrot

"Well. What I'm suggesting is that. We launch... let's say a small expeditionary force to take the islands and make them a Special District of Floueschia. No people live there, so it's not colonialism per say. And, there is a giant deposit of crude oil. Huge deposit, actually. So what do you say, Muller? Interesting, right?" He said, boasting, handing over another proposal for administering the islands as a Special Administrative Region, which effectively would be a district without its own devolved government and administered directly by Staatsrot. As well as potential sites for oil drilling to begin. 

"Well. Fuelenger, it's not a horrible idea. We won't look bad for this because there aren't people there, the islands aren't in a bad location either...I think we could probably get this through the Staatsrot. What do you define as a "Small Expeditionary Force" Though?"

Muller says curious on how much he's actually going to have to commit to this

"Oh. That? I think the Fallschiermjäger and maybe an Infantry Brigade would be capable of securing the islands. No? Fallschiermjäger goes in first, secures a beachhead on one or all of the islands, then we land an infantry brigade and claim the islands. They can be back before we even cross into Nevonia."

Muller begins to look over each of the documents, Fuelenger waiting eagerly to see if he will actually approve his plan. Finally muller looks up, and then back at Fuelenger

"Fine. You got your approval. Go ahead and call the Inspector General and work something out with him. Ill talk to the Staatsrot about your SAV and Annexation proposal." Muller says, preparing to sign off on his folder

"Actually. Muller. I need one more thing. Humor me. Right? So, the Lavanians?. There...a friendly republic, right? We're going to need a base, at least temporarily for air support and to keep a steady stream of reliable supply going. Let me go to them and ask if they're willing to make a behind-the-door deal."

Muller sighs

"Fine. Go ahead. Just don't get caught. I'm sure you already know what the Radical Republicans would think about it."

__________________________________________________________________________

[spoiler=Secure Communication]

From: Acting Secretariat of National Defense, Gonthier Fuelenger of the Second Flouesch Republic

To: Whom it may concern within the Government of the United Lavian Republic

I am reaching out on behalf of the First Consul of the Second Flouesch Republic, Fredrick Muller

Within the coming weeks, the Flouesch Republic will embark on an expeditionary mission to islands directly south of your country. Given that they are internationally nameless, we are, for the purposes of clear communication, going to name them the "Avalonian Islands". It may come as no surprise to my counterpart within the United Lavian Republic that, due to circumstances outside of my control, the republic currently has no open sea navy within its possession. Therefore, we are requesting what exactly you would demand in return for a quasi-secret military access deal that would allow our air force to operate within your country. Specifically, being allowed to use bases within your country so they may deploy paratroopers to the islands to be the primary Vanguard of the Expeditionary Force. 

Additionally. We are willing to negotiate the purchase of potentially 1 assault ship to ferry over infantry soldiers to the islands once the paratrooper landings have commenced in full. We are also potentially interested in the acquisition of air-to-air refueling vehicles as our current stockpile of said aircraft is quite limited in there numbers and capabilities. 

Respectfully, Acting Secretariat of National Defense, Gonthier Fuelenger

Fräiheet, Fridden, Brout a Rosen.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler= [b]A message received, a message sent[/b]]
David Witstrom sat in his ancient office chair, sipping from some fruity carbonated drink the vending machine recently stocked as he finished up his workday. His mind drifted from the recent reports he was reviewing about the ongoing conflict in Astanir and military exports to Italian-Dutch to the beverage. It was green apple flavored. Sweet but sour with the carbonation only emphasizing the latter, quite the change from the energy drink or coffee he was accustomed to at the time. He thought to himself about if the ministry was attempting to be more healthy or if it was some new craze with the younger people, but he could care less. The drink was good, and maybe hed try one of the other flavors tomorrow.

His screen, going into powersaving mode due to his inactivity, set itself back to its standard brightness, drawing his attention back from his thoughts to a new notification from his email. Who is it now? Some defence contractor wanting to make another bid for another project? Or hell, maybe even one more of these blasted reports hell have to mull over and attempt to remember. After some time of attempting to navigate through the forest which was his mountain of open tabs, he gave up and simply opened a new window to access it.  What he found waiting for him however, immediately drew his attention better than those dry reports.

A foreign message, apparently from one Gonthier Fuelenger about the Flouesch Republic wanting to mount some ambitious expedition to some islands near the southeastern coast of mainland Vespuria, and almost a straight shot west of Lavia if you give or take a few degrees. The letter asked for some quasi-secret access deal to allow their airforce to operate inside of Lavia to deploy paratroopers to the islands, with the addition of talking about somehow purchasing an assault ship and some mid-air refueling aircraft. 

Who the hell just spats that out? He re-read the message another time over before asking himself further questions. Why paratroopers? Thats insanely costly, not to mention the need to somehow get food and other things to those men as they established some sort of port on the islands. Seconds later, his brain answered itself. Their navy ran off after that coup. They literally have no other way of getting meant over there without commandeering some civilian ships not at all built for the task. Even a better question, why the hell would they want to be down there? The Secretariat of National Defense had omitted any reasoning for the request in his little message.

Swiveling in his office chair, he pressed down upon a button on his desk phone, immediately talking to his assistant on the other side of his office door. He knew exactly who to consult with at a time like this, a close friend from his time in the Marine Commandos. Jeane, get Carlos Tapin at Makinar Military Intelligence Command on the secure line. I need a word with him. After ending the message, Witstrom picked up the receiver on an ancient looking red colored phone, the one which provided an uninterrupted line buried far underground straight to the MMIC. 

After a few seconds of nothing, he heard the recognizable click of the line becoming active, the signature accent he knew well transmitting over the distance. Bonjour Ministre, I was just about to ring you as well. Did you get this crap thing too? Witstrom grumbled over the phone. Either someone had accessed very secure email accounts just to play a prank, or this was some wild new way of trying to conduct international business. Yes David, I got it as well. What do you make of it? After thinking for a second, Witstrom gave an answer. I make of it that some punk- he didnt get another word out before being cut off by Tapin. Détendez-vous, my dear friend. Ive had one of our men here in the Vespruian department to investigate this with the current information we have, and it's possible that this could be real. Ambitious and perhaps a bit foolish, but possible that those Floueshcians dont have the best relation with the major oil exporters near them, and their recent revolution could leave them wanting more independent production.

Witstrom pondered this possibility for a minute or two, then responded roughly. Carlos, I know you're a smart man, not to mention younger. I want you to get a message to this so-called Secretariat of National Defense that if their nation wants to talk, they forgo all this secret crap and have a meeting directly. Im not involving us with some nation who would gladly send their communist goons to terrorize us like they did to their own. The President and his advisors can talk it out with this archaic nation. After a few seconds, he added We can talk more of this when any update comes of it. Make sure your agents get the message through to the right man. 

After his small rant, he could hear Carlos chuckling on the other end of the line. No worries, Ministre. With a nation this disorganized, a schoolboy could get into their secure facilities. Ill make sure it happens, friend. Talk to you over seafood on the weekend. With that, the line went dead once again. Sarcastic bastard, no wonder they were still friends. Witstrom stood up and finished off his drink. It was time to leave this up to the career politicians and let him have some rest.
[/spoiler]

The yellow represents the unlivable, dry land from the affects of the nuclear fallout. The three red triangles represent a simplified nuclear symbol. The blue strips on the sides represent how hope for peace is still somewhat there.

[Spoiler=[u][b]The Enclave Intelligence Mission[/b][/u]]
[i]
John Zurkic, an operative of the Enclave S.S. or the Secret Sekuceania Forces, an elite branch of the Enclave Intelligence Bureau, was known for his precision and ruthless efficiency. His latest assignment was one of the most critical yet to track down the fugitive known only as Mr. Fox

The room smelled of rust and bleach. A single bulb swung above, its faint light cutting shadows across the steel walls. John Zurkic leaned against the far side of the chamber, his black Enclave S.S. coat heavy on his shoulders. He didnt move, didnt speak. He only watched.

The man tied to the chair was trembling. His face was swollen, his lips split, and blood streaked his jaw. Mr. Foxs husband is nothing more than a tool to the Bureau now.

One of Zurkics fellow officers tipped a steel pitcher and poured water across the mans face. He choked, gagging as the liquid filled his nose and mouth. The sound scraped against Johns nerves. He had seen it all before. Torture was just another method. Yet something about the desperation in the mans eyes felt different.

The iron door opened with a clang. Two guards dragged in a boy no older than nine. His small wrists strained against the soldiers grip, his wide eyes flicking between his father and the men in black uniforms.

The husband thrashed in his bonds. No! Leave him out of this!
Zurkic straightened. His jaw tightened. This wasnt a procedure. Not with children.

The lead officer, a tall man with a scar splitting his cheek, grabbed the boy by the shoulder and forced him forward. He pressed a blade against the boys throat, the steel glinting in the harsh light.
Talk, the officer growled. Or your son dies in front of you!

The husbands screams filled the chamber. He pulled so hard at the restraints that blood seeped from his wrists. His eyes met his sons, filled with helpless terror.
Johns hand twitched near the holster at his side. He wanted to step in, to tell them this was too far. But the Enclave S.S. wasnt made for showing mercy. His orders were clear. Extract information, whatever the cost He clenched his fists, forcing himself still.

Finally, broken, the man sobbed. Stop! Please, stopIll tell you where he is!
The blade lowered, just slightly.

The husband gasped for breath, tears streaming down his battered face. Hes gone. He he went up west. The United Lavian Republic. The capital New Rorack. Thats where youll find him.
A hush fell over the room. The officer released the boy and shoved him back into the arms of the guards. With trembling fingers, the man scribbled the location on a crumpled scrap of paper.
John took the note, folding it neatly into his coat pocket. He didnt look at the husband, nor at the boy. Instead, he turned toward the door. New Rorack, he thought grimly. Thats where the hunt begins.

The train slid into the station with a shriek of iron on iron, brakes biting against the rails. John Zurkic sat stiffly in his seat, a long black coat covering the pistol strapped under his arm. Outside the window, the skyline of New Rorack rose into view, with sharp spires of glass and steel cutting into the gray sky, streets buzzing with trams and merchant carts.

It was different from the Enclave. Here, the flag of the United Lavian Republic bore a hawk, not an eagle like the Enclave Flag. The people moved with a kind of ease he hadnt seen.
John stepped onto the platform. He blended in easily enough; to them, he was just another foreign businessman. His forged papers gave him a new identity of Karel Vinter, a textile importer from Osvaren Province. The Enclave S.S. made sure of it.

He adjusted his collar and walked through the crowded terminal. His mind turned to the note still tucked inside his coat pocket...the last words of Mr. Foxs husband, scrawled in shaky handwriting. New Rorack. Thats where youll find him.

As he crossed the busy square outside the station, he kept scanning the faces. Every man in a coat, every woman glancing too long his wayone of them could be a watcher.
He ducked into a side café, ordering a bitter Lavian coffee and sitting by the window. He didnt drink. His eyes followed the street, his mind replaying the interrogation chamber. The boys wide, terrified eyes wouldnt leave him.

This mission is it about stopping a rebellion? Or about silencing a man who dares to resist?

Mr. Vinter?

The voice broke his thoughts. A woman in her thirties stood by his table, her dark hair tied neatly, a parcel tucked under her arm. She smiled faintly, but her eyes were sharp.
John kept his tone flat. You have the delivery?

She set the parcel down. Inside, wrapped in plain cloth, lay a dossier. Contacts, safehouses, and a photographgrainy, black and white. The figure in the photo was unmistakable: narrow eyes. A sharp jawline. The long coat of a man who knew how to vanish in a crowd.

Mr. Fox

Johns hand lingered on the picture. Somewhere in this city, Fox was hiding a rally of his people, planning the next strike against the Enclave. Could it be that these States hold support for Mr. Fox? It would make sense, since the Enclave and ULR had been long-time enemies, even back in the old regime era.

The woman leaned closer. Careful, agent. New Rorack isnt the Enclave. If the Lavian authorities catch you here, your government will deny you even exist.
John slipped the photo into his coat. His jaw tightened. Then Ill make sure they never see me.
He rose, leaving the untouched coffee behind.
